summary: Open any file — even multi-gigabyte — and scroll / filter / derive / export it. Windowed, read-only over the source, offline.

reach.network: none — the verified lamina.html artifact (this file) makes zero network requests; connect-src 'none' enforces it

hosted_pwa.note: gentropic.org/lamina (and the MS Store package) wraps this artifact in a PWA shell (index.html + a service worker) that is OUTSIDE this sealed file. The SW runs in its own context (not bound by the page's connect-src) and fetches ONLY same-origin app assets (offline shell cache) + an update check ('is there a newer build?'). It never accesses opened file data — that stays in the page's memory, never handed to the SW — so data confidentiality is unaffected. For provable zero-network, run this downloaded lamina.html from file:// (no SW). Update UI in the app drives the SW via postMessage, not a page fetch, so connect-src none still holds.
hosted_pwa.network: same-origin app assets + update check only

filesystem.reads: user-opened files only (picker / drag-drop / a recent, which re-grants permission)
filesystem.writes: user-initiated export only, to a user-chosen path (OS Save dialog)
filesystem.local_state: block-index cache + an optional recents list (file handles + names) in IndexedDB — local only, never transmitted; reopening a recent re-grants permission (no silent re-read); clearable + disableable
